content:
Principle My principle includes a diagram that helps determine whether a task should be left for humans, automated, AI automated or be hybrid (human-in-loop).
Problem Organizations are adopting generative AI but used sometimes in scenarios that contradict with the desired business outcomes and lead to losses.
Diagram https://zenodo.org/records/24320246/files/mousa-principle-automation-v1_signed.pdf?download=1
Rationale
My diagram lays out a principle that will help in distinguishing between automation, AI and clarifies where humans should be kept in loop. Also, it clarifies when for certain business cases its better to keep certain tasks fully human.
Definitions Human: The task should be handled fully by humans.
Automation: This means a code or program that follows traditional software development standards.
AI: This means the task is passed on to generative AI for processing.
Hybrid: This means that whether you choose AI or automation, a human must be involved for critical operations.
Example According to Castelo et al. (2023), consumers evaluated the same service interaction less favorably when they were told they were interacting with a chatbot rather than a human employee. My diagram makes it clear that roles expecting human empathy should not be delegated to machines or non-humans.
Scope and limitations My principle applies to common commercial use cases. It does not apply to defense related use cases.
Related work The ISO/IEC 42001 already addresses certain parts surrounding AI including ethics, human-in-loop. However my diagram is for practical use by decision makers and helps translate technical concepts into everyday business language to assist decision makers in making informed decisions.
Note The version 1.0 write-up and diagram are archived on Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/24320246
summary: Determining whether a task should be delegated to AI, automated or left for humans can be tough. This is why I created Mousa Automation Principle V1 that helps decision makers decide what path to use.
title: Mousa Automation Principle V1

content:
I’m happy to announce launching my new personal blog.
I was inspired to create my own personal website when LinkedIn asked me to send them my passport to verify my account. This raised real concerns regarding our privacy and data.
Fast forward, I created finally my website where you can find information about me as well as professional background instead of LinkedIn.
I can argue that there is not much of a difference between having your profile on a personal website and LinkedIn with the latter being slightly worse in terms of privacy and lack of transparency.
My website will be the main source of truth in regards to content I post about tech, advocacy and other topics; and I hope that in future everyone will be able to create their own website and have sovereignty over their digital representation on the web.
Please note that I do not represent any organization.
